explanation: Standard form Ax + By = C hides the slope but makes the intercepts easy. Setting y = 0 gives the x-intercept at C/A (green), and setting x = 0 gives the y-intercept at C/B (red) — slide A, B, C and watch both intercept dots slide along the axes. The slope is always −A/B, shown live, so you can read steepness right off the coefficients.
bullets: x-intercept is C/A (let y = 0); y-intercept is C/B (let x = 0).
The slope of Ax + By = C is always −A/B.
Plotting the two intercepts and connecting them draws the whole line.
